subject: Fail to factorize Q. (Spatial, distance, generic0)

messages.author: c4a3575d08613e47
messages.subject: Fail to factorize Q. (Spatial, distance, generic0)
parts:
Hi there. I'm trying to run a spatial model based on the relative (inverse) distance of a set of neighbors. My model specification is this

formula = GP_udg_sygsik ~ f(location,model="generic0",Cmatrix=Cmat + X
model = inla(formula, family = "gaussian", data=data, verbose=TRUE)

where Cmat is attached, and X is a matrix of 71 covariates. I've also attached the data and my R-script.

summary(model) shows that the coefficient of the 71 covariates are all very close to zero (but seemingly not actually zero). Clearly something is wrong here. model$ok is TRUE, but Verbose=T shows this error:


file: smtp-taucs.c  hgid: 15fa1e788b12  date: Fri Sep 20 09:14:11 2013 +0200
Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 829, Thread: 0
Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

This error repeats lord knows how many times. Whats going on here?

Kind regards, Claus Vestergaard

parts:
I've standardised the  rows, so the row sums of C is, per definition, 1. For some reason I was convinced that diagonal-elements of Cmat should be forced =0. Silly me. Anyway I've set the diag(Cmat) <- -1*rowSums(Cmat) (attached). This seems to solve the problem somewhat. Now the estimates are much more reasonable, although INLA still goes through the "..try to fix it" step many times.

You mentioned negative off-diagonals, ie. a negative weight for the inverse distance? Please elaborate...


Regards, Claus

> I've standardised the rows, so the row sums of C is, per definition,
> 1. For some reason I was convinced that diagonal-elements of Cmat
> should be forced =0. Silly me. Anyway I've set the diag(Cmat) <-
> -1*rowSums(Cmat) (attached). This seems to solve the problem somewhat.
> Now the estimates are much more reasonable, although INLA still goes
> through the "..try to fix it" step many times.
>
>
> You mentioned negative off-diagonals, ie. a negative weight for the
> inverse distance? Please elaborate...
>

I think you got the sign of Cmat wrong, the diagonal must be > 0 and
offdiaginal term are 'usually' < 0, can you try setting Cmat=-Cmat ?

also since each row sums to zero, then its intrinsic and you should
either remove the intercept or setting

f(..., diag = 1e-6, constr=TRUE)

forcing it to have sum-to-zero constraint.

H

--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Fail to factorize Q. (Spatial, distance, generic0)
parts:
On 29/04/14 15:10, Claus H. Vestergaard wrote:
> If by "how singular it is" you mean how many eigenvalues are zero, the
> answer is 9 out of 270 = 3.3%. What do i do with this information?

That's more than I expected (=1). Do you have several disconnected
components in the graph?

But the magnitude of the eigenvalues is also of interest; for
non-singular matrices, the ratio between the largest and smallest
eigenvalue determines the condition number, which tells us something
about how bad the numerics will be.

Finn
